items.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, November 11, 2017 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I did get to meet some people who I was knocked out to meet like Max Roach and Lou Donaldson and Mose Allison and I got to work with Walter Bishop Junior and Lou

ctx.x: Yeah. A very long time ago I got to sit in with Lou Donaldson because the bass player that I knew was playing with Lou. And he said, “Hey man, let this cat sit in.” This was a long time ago. And Lou at first didn’t know me, why would he have me sit in? And the bass player kept making it — and I’m like, “Please leave Lou alone.” And he finally did bring me up. And I know that Lou plays a lot of Charlie Parker. So I said, “Can we do ‘Lady Be Good’?” And I sang “Lady Be Good,” and then Lou played a solo, and then I…

“Well, for me that’s one of Charlie Parker’s most well-constructed solos. And then here’s the punch line. He said, “But he had to play something, because he was standing next to Lester Young.” So that put the whole thing into context for me. Not only was it a great solo, but I didn’t know that when he played that solo it was at Jazz at the Philharmonic and Prez was on the gig. And Charlie Parker was very young at the time, or relatively young, and he knew that he was going to be playing with his idol, Lester…

items.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 29, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Lou Donaldson saying, “yeah man, come on up.” You know. “Yeah a friend of mine, come on up and sing a tune, Gates.”

ctx.x: Somebody asked him, they said, “I’d like to take a lesson with you in improvisation.” And Chet, who is a little salty sometimes, said, “well improvisation is about imagination or lack of it.” So I always remembered that. You’d better have something to say, otherwise don’t say much. Say a little then get out. A long, long time ago I went to a jam session at a club in Seaford, Long Island called Sonny’s Place. It was a club that was there for many years and many great players and singers stopped in there just to…

another one.” I said, “yes indeed.” So to be accepted by somebody who I looked up to, I wouldn’t have cared if he threw me off the bandstand. Because that’s what they do. But to be accepted like that is like just huge for me. I mean I drove home, it was like a two hour drive home, I’m going like, “wow, Billy Mitchell said it was okay.” And then I got a gig, about three months later. He [Sonny] gave me a date that night, for three months down the road. And I showed up with a rhythm section with guys that I knew…
